title: The Anatomy of Pain
subtitle: Give me a remedy that sends me into slumber, or better yet, back to the good old days.

items.text: The Anatomy of Pain
Rehab Center, Laplace

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: No! Toa, brother!

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: I ... I'm coming to save you!

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: The storm is coming. The shell ... our island ...

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: I'm sorry.
Fatutu lies on the examination bed, eyes shut tight, brow furrowed, mumbling in her sleep, fighting against the weight of her dream.
Rehab Center Hallway, Laplace

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: It's strange to see Miss Fatutu look like this. I don't know if I've ever seen her so troubled.
She peers through the window, watching with quiet worry.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper, it's strange. When she's awake, she never shows any sadness at all.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Even when she first submitted her request, she didn't seem afraid or sad. It felt oddly clinical, like she was only asking for cough syrup.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: She's been so warm and kind to everyone here. She never let on about this, even as she was doing so much to help others.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I suppose I just don't understand her. If she's hurting so much inside, why wouldn't she let us know?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper, could it be that she still doesn't trust us?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Asking for our help may not be her first instinct right now.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: The Foundation looks out for everyone. All she had to do was ask.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I had hoped she would want to be friends.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'm sure she does, in her own way. We just need to give her more time.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We'll be here for her. But she has to settle in first—learn to feel safe.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Understood.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Let's hope Mesmer Jr.'s Artificial Somnambulism Therapy can help Miss Fatutu recover.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: You may not want to set your expectations too high. This treatment is far from a panacea.
The therapist steps out from the recovery room, pristine as ever, speaking plainly and without pretense.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: I evaluated this "patient" earlier. I had been preparing to guide her into a dream state, but before I could begin, she had already entered one on her own.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: It's just as you see there.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: But there's nothing so complex about her nightmares. Nothing that requires Artificial Somnambulism Therapy.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: This is nothing less than pure and unfiltered homesickness.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Is there any other way to ease Miss Fatutu's pain?

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Ease her pain?

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: As I said, you may be overestimating our capabilities, or perhaps I should say underestimating the nature of her suffering.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: I would never argue that Artificial Somnambulism Therapy is anything other than a remarkable leap in science.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: It's helped correct behavioral issues caused by the "Storm"—paranoia, compulsions, violence—those things, yes.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: But it can't erase or even relieve the pain.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: At best, dream-guiding might offer a momentary distraction from the nightmares, but it would be a false comfort—escapism.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: We can't rely on Artificial Somnambulism to save her.
The rebuke leaves no room for argument.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Miss Mesmer, are you saying you won't treat Fatutu?

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: I'm saying I have no treatment suitable for her.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: All I can offer is some help falling asleep.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: I wouldn't recommend anything more than a hot bath and a cup of warm milk.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I see.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: She'll wake soon. Despite what I've said, I believe she is capable of overcoming her pain. But there's nothing more I can do to help.
With that, the no-nonsense therapist turns and walks away, leaving no opening for further questions.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Fatutu ...
Her gaze lingers on the girl beside her. Then, without a word, she looks away again—quietly, unnoticed.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: There must be something we can do.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Let me think.
Some things can't be undone. Like glass shattered across the floor, too broken to piece back together.
Their present problem seems just as daunting. Side by side, the two lean against the wall in silence.
They're searching for a way to heal something as abstract as "heartache."
Yet suddenly, footsteps interrupt their thoughts—light, hurried, like wind chimes jingling with urgency.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Fatutu!

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Where is Fatutu? Is she in there?
She grabs a sleeve, then someone's hand, eyes wide with concern.
Before anyone can answer, she's already flung herself toward the window, peering in at Fatutu lying on the recovery bed.
She presses up to the glass.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Fatutu, wake up! Fatutu ...

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Ms. Barcarola.
Sonetto starts to step forward, but a hand reaches out to stop her. Her superior gives a slight shake of the head—wait.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: I have something very important to tell you, Fatutu!
Her voice reaches through. Fatutu stirs from her bed, her eyes flutter open softly, searching for the calling voice.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: You're awake! Fatutu!
She leaps toward her like a dolphin sailing up over sunlit waves, in an irrepressible motion.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Barcarola?

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Chiaro, who else would it be?

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Time to wake up. There's something far more important than sleeping to be done now!

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: What is it?

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: It's trade season!

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: The trade season is just about to begin!
